_comment: Hand-placed and hand-corrected positions for A8, in pixels of
.build/a8/drawing_full.png (5350x3010) and of the schN_full.png crops.
The board read well: 144 of 187 designators, 112 of them in the agreed
tier. Every one of the 144 was rendered onto the drawing and looked at.
Fifteen were wrong and are corrected here -- C2, C6, C7, C16, CR5, L2,
R13, R17, T1, U1, U2, U9, U10, Z2 and TP5, which the reader read off the
TP9 label (the 9-as-S confusion the pitfalls describe). Twenty-eight more
the reader never found are placed by eye off a pixel grid.
All ten test points are placed by hand whatever the reader thought, and
every box spans the silkscreen label AND its wire-loop pad. On this board
the pad sits about 45 px below and 30 px left of its label -- a marker
centred on the text alone sends a probe to the wrong hole.
TP3 is the odd one out: its label is vertical and its pad is a vertical
bar immediately to the right of the text rather than below it.
The photo alignment is marked approximate. Six landmark pairs were
measured, all on flat in-plane silkscreen -- part outlines where the photo
shows one, and lettering only where the drawing and the board agree on
where it sits. The ejector ears, the two standoffs and the mounting-hole
hardware are deliberately not used; they stand proud of the board. Worst
landmark residual is 4.1 photo px and two independent check features (the
U1 DIP corner and the C22 body) land within 16 px, but nothing under the
MP2 hybrid cover could be anchored at all, so positions in that corner are
the homography's word rather than a measurement.
_sheetsComment: Zone grid frames. The inner frame -- the rule just inside the zone-label
band -- was located from the ink profile of each full-resolution crop
rather than by eye, because every sheet sits at a different offset and
each is scanned with a fraction of a degree of skew. Columns run 8 to 1
left to right and rows D to A top to bottom on all five sheets.
_boardComment: Centre and size in pixels of drawing_full.png. Everything here is
'verified' -- it was looked at on the full-resolution drawing.

_notOnDrawingComment: Parts with no silkscreen designator of their own, so they can never be
placed and counting them as unplaced would make the coverage badge lie.
H5-H8 are rivets, MP18-MP21 soluble spacers, MP9/MP10 the nylon ejectors
(drawn as the corner ears, but unlabelled), and MP2 the moulded cover over
the hybrid. C32 is the odd one: it is a real 220 pF part in the 1996 parts
list, but it appears in no Rev 9 list, on no schematic sheet and nowhere on
the locator drawing, so there is no position to give it.
_layersComment: src is board/drawing space and dst is photo space; H maps board -> photo.
Six pairs, measured on flat in-plane silkscreen only.
_dropSchematicComment: Every marker the reader produced on a sheet was rendered and looked at on
sheet 1, and the result is the pitfalls file's warning in numbers: of 96
reads, 25 were right. The rest sat on relay bottom-view legend captions
('K1, K3-K6, K13, K15-K20, K22, K24, K25' is eight designators in a row and
not one of them is a position), on the transistor package legends, on the
test point legend table, on pin numbers, on net names, on the notes block
and on the title block's '(1 of 5)'. Everything not on the reviewed keep
list is dropped here. Two of sheet 1's own drops are worth naming because
they look like parts and are not: C4 and C6 are the zone references in
'(PG3 C4)' and '(PG3 C6)' in the test point legend, and Q6/Q7/Q9/Q10/Q12/
Q13/Q1/Q2/Q4/U3 are the captions of the bottom-view package legends.
Sheets 2, 3 and 4 have now been reviewed the same way, marker by marker,
and the hit rate matches sheet 1's shape: sheet 2 kept 24 of 62, sheet 3
36 of 68, sheet 4 78 of 125 -- the relay coil labels on sheet 4 read almost
perfectly, while the capacitor and IC reads on sheets 2 and 3 were mostly
pin numbers, net names and neighbouring labels. What is still listed here
was looked at and is wrong. A marker that is not there cannot send anyone
to the wrong part; one that is there and wrong can.
Sheet 5 gets no reader pass at all and has no entry here. It is nothing but
the relay/FET state table -- rows of ranges against columns headed K1..K33,
Q6, Q7, Q9/Q10, Q11 -- plus its legend and the title block. There is no
circuit body on it, so every read it could produce would be a column header
that names a part without saying where it is. A14's sheet 4 is the same
shape and is handled the same way.
_schematicComment: Hand placements on the sheets. All ten test points are placed on the net,
beside the flag symbol, and each was checked against the signal name the
sheet prints next to it -- 'S COM' beside TP9, 'ZERO OUT' beside TP6 -- which
is a check independent of the reader. The sheet and zone were read off the
sheet 1 legend first (TP1 = DC ATT INPUT (PG3 D6) and so on) and every one
of the ten landed in the zone the legend names.
The rest are parts, and they come in three kinds. Some promote a reader hit
the eye confirmed, so the badge stops reporting a disagreement that has been
settled -- these are mostly the collision tier, which build_coords skips even
when the read is right, because two names landed on one label. Some correct a
read that had the position right and the name wrong: the reader called CR10
'CR12', CR9 'CR1', R9 'R5', Q13 'Q1'. The rest are labels the reader never
found in the circuit body at all -- the four chokes L1-L4, T1, U9, U10, U20,
Q6, Q7 and their neighbours -- placed by eye off the full-resolution sheet.
Every box in this section was rendered back onto the sheet and looked at.
H2 is the one part in the assembly the sheets do not name; its entry says so.
